title: Power, Gas, and LNG Trading: Racing to Compete in the Coming Decade
gist: BCG argues that by 2035 the profit pool in power, gas, and LNG trading will have rotated decisively out of curve/asset-backed and customer-flow models into proprietary risk-taking (already up to 40% of value) and short-term asset-backed trading (10% to 15%+ of value), because renewables growth of 8-12% per year, negative prices ~8% of hours in Germany/Netherlands, and 15-minute European settlement have made human-led trading impossible. The winners will be data-centric, systematically trading firms (Citadel, Vitol, InCommodities, Danske Commodities are named as the aggressors); incumbents face a $100M+ multiyear rebuild where 70% of the value comes from operating-model change, not tools.

insights.claim: In Germany and the Netherlands, wholesale power prices are negative roughly 8% of the time, meaning companies are paid to consume or store power — a structural feature, not an anomaly, created by renewable surges onto the grid.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: An 8% negative-price duty cycle is the direct economic basis for battery/flexibility asset returns in Northwest Europe; underwrite storage revenue stacks against this frequency rather than against average spreads.
insights.quote: Roughly 8% of the time in these two countries, companies are being paid to consume or store power.
insights.locator: Market volatility and shorter trading windows explain

insights.claim: Europe now mandates 15-minute settlement intervals in day-ahead power markets, while the US is moving more slowly and less uniformly via the ramp-up of day-ahead, real-time (DART) trading.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Granularity is a regulatory forcing function for algo capability: European desks are being pushed onto systematic infrastructure ahead of US peers, which advantages EU-native traders and vendors of high-frequency ETRM/optimization tooling.
insights.locator: On the regulatory side, Europe now requires

insights.claim: As episodic volatility becomes harder to predict and trading windows shrink, discretionary human trading is no longer viable in power and gas — algorithms, short-term optimization, and systematic trading have gone mainstream.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Treat 'discretionary energy desk' as a declining business model; capability screens for utilities and merchant traders should weight quant headcount and automation coverage over trader pedigree.
insights.quote: human-led trading has become impossible
insights.locator: As extreme episodic volatility becomes harder to predict

insights.claim: Renewables are growing 8% to 12% per year globally, far faster than demand growth, which pushes price formation toward intermittent supply and local grid conditions and moves the money into intraday markets while curve volatility becomes harder to monetize.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The renewables-vs-demand growth gap is the single mechanism behind the intraday value shift — a direct read-through for who wins between forward-curve houses and intraday/flex specialists.
insights.quote: As renewables grow at 8% to 12% per year globally, far faster than demand growth, market prices have become increasingly sensitive to intermittent supply and local grid conditions.
insights.locator: Markets Are Moving Faster Than Incumbents Expected

insights.claim: LNG has become the world's price-setting mechanism for gas, and European and Asian prices now move much more in lockstep than five years ago because Europe replaced Russian pipeline gas with internationally sourced LNG.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: TTF-JKM correlation is now structural rather than episodic, which compresses the classic inter-basin arb and raises the beta of European industrial gas costs to Asian weather and demand shocks.
insights.quote: LNG has become the world’s price-setting mechanism, and European and Asian prices now move much more in lockstep than they did five years ago.
insights.locator: In gas and LNG, the big shift is geographic

insights.claim: European storage and time-arbitrage spreads have narrowed, so gas trading value has migrated toward sourcing physical cargoes, managing portfolio optionality, and reacting fast to dislocations.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Storage-lease-and-carry strategies in Europe are a shrinking pool; edge sits with players holding cargo optionality and the speed to act, favoring integrated portfolio traders over pure storage optimizers.
insights.locator: In Europe, the spreads that made storage and time arbitrage profitable

insights.claim: A conflict in the Middle East at the start of 2026 produced gas and LNG market dislocations that rewarded traders able to act swiftly, and BCG cites early 2026 as a period when both outsized gains and outsized losses occurred.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Recent P&L dispersion in energy trading is crisis-driven, not skill-uniform — screen 2026 trading results for one-off geopolitical windfalls before extrapolating run-rate earnings for utility trading arms.
insights.quote: as they did early in 2026 at the start of the conflict in the Middle East
insights.locator: In Europe, the spreads that made storage and time arbitrage profitable

insights.claim: LNG demand growth of 2% to 3% per year in Asia-Pacific and Latin America plus market liberalization is opening new demand centers and new trading value pools, while North America's rising export capacity ties regional gas markets further into the global market.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Growth in LNG trading value is emerging-market-demand-led; exposure to new Asian and Latin American offtake and to US export capacity is the growth leg, not European volumes.
insights.locator: Market liberalization and LNG demand growth of 2% to 3%

insights.claim: BCG expects power and LNG markets to drive long-term growth in energy trading while gas value pools come under pressure, especially in Europe.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A clean allocation signal within commodity trading: overweight power and LNG desks/exposure, underweight European gas-centric franchises.
insights.quote: we expect power and LNG markets to drive long-term growth in energy trading, while gas value pools will be under pressure, especially in Europe
insights.locator: Given more volatile power markets and further liberalization

themes.theme: Value Pool Rotation Across Five Business Models

insights.claim: Proprietary trading and risk taking already accounts for up to 40% of total power and gas trading value across all market participants, including hedge funds and global merchant traders, and is expected to grow further.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The largest and growing slice of energy-trading profit is speculative risk-taking, not asset service — which raises earnings volatility for any listed utility leaning into it and explains the hedge-fund incursion.
insights.quote: Proprietary trading and risk taking already accounts for up to 40% of total power and gas trading value by all market participants
insights.locator: Proprietary trading and risk taking already accounts

insights.claim: Proprietary trading will grow partly because banks are largely absent from power and gas trading, especially in Europe, leaving prop desks as the necessary providers of curve liquidity.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Bank retrenchment is a structural subsidy to non-bank energy traders' returns; any regulatory re-entry by banks into commodity risk would compress that edge.
insights.quote: proprietary trading will simply be necessary to provide market liquidity on the curve, since many banks are not active in power and gas trading, especially in Europe
insights.locator: First of all, proprietary trading will simply be necessary

insights.claim: Short-term asset-backed trading is the fastest-growing segment, expected to rise from roughly 10% of total value today to 15% or more by 2035 as flexible demand and new wind capacity push activity into day-ahead, intraday, ancillary, and real-time markets.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A quantified ten-year growth vector: build or buy capability in intraday/ancillary optimization and VPP aggregation, where the addressable pool grows ~50%+ in relative share.
insights.quote: expected to increase from roughly 10% of total value today to 15% or more by 2035
insights.locator: Short-term asset-backed trading is the fastest-growing segment

insights.claim: Asset-backed trading on the curve will decline in relative importance as renewables take generation share, though hydro portfolios and selected flexible assets hold their value because traders can keep trading around them as forward prices shift.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Hydro flexibility is called out as the durable exception in a shrinking category — a specific quality screen for Nordic/Alpine utility asset bases versus thermal-curve-dependent ones.
insights.locator: Asset-backed trading on the curve remains a large pool

insights.claim: Flexibility purchase agreements covering third-party batteries and small generators grew to more than 10 gigawatts of contracted capacity in Europe in 2025, versus less than 5 gigawatts in previous years — more than a doubling.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: FPAs are the fastest-scaling new contract structure in European power; the doubling in 2025 is a hard datapoint for battery developers' route-to-market and for traders monetizing third-party flexibility.
insights.quote: In Europe, these agreements covered more than 10 gigawatts of capacity contracted in 2025, compared with less than 5 gigawatts in previous years.
insights.locator: Origination and structuring remain relevant

insights.claim: Customer flow business is only around 5% of total power and gas trading value and faces the greatest pressure, with margins squeezed by competition, regulation, and the price sensitivity of large offtakers.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Retail/B2B energy supply franchises are structurally the weakest link in the trading value chain — a margin-compression short thesis for pure-play flow intermediaries.
insights.quote: Customer flow business remains a relatively small share, at around 5% of total value, and faces the greatest pressure.
insights.locator: Customer flow business remains a relatively small share

themes.theme: Attackers, Incumbents, and the 2035 Operating Model

insights.claim: Citadel, Vitol, InCommodities, and Danske Commodities have expanded aggressively into power and gas, treating data as a strategic asset, deploying probabilistic analytics and systematic signal generation at scale, automating the trade life cycle, and beginning to deploy agentic AI.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: These four are named as the competitive benchmark — market-share loss by European utility trading arms should be attributed to them, and their capability set defines the required investment bar.
insights.quote: firms such as Citadel, Vitol, InCommodities, and Danske Commodities have expanded aggressively into power and gas
insights.locator: Additional pressure comes from a changing competitive landscape

insights.claim: The best-in-class 2035 trading organization will be built on a unified real-time data platform treating data as the primary productive asset — explicitly not a heavily customized ETRM system with analytics bolted on — with cross-functional trader/quant/engineer teams replacing siloed desks.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A direct negative signal for incumbent ETRM vendors whose value rests on customization, and a positive one for data-platform-first architectures in commodity trading tech spend.
insights.quote: not a heavily customized energy trading and risk management system with analytics bolted on, but a platform that treats data as the primary productive asset
insights.locator: A Vision for 2035

insights.claim: Agentic AI operating autonomously within guardrails will entirely change middle- and back-office operations in trading firms, and that shift is only just beginning.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Mid/back-office headcount and outsourced trade-support providers are the first automation casualties in energy trading; the timing is called early-stage, so the disruption is ahead not behind.
insights.quote: Agentic AI, systems that act autonomously within guardrails, will entirely change how middle- and back-office operations work. That shift is only just beginning.
insights.locator: Leading Players. These organizations are moving beyond

themes.theme: Transformation Economics: Cost of Entry and Payoff

insights.claim: A legacy incumbent's radical transformation to a unified data foundation connecting trading, analytics, and operations could easily exceed $100 million as a multiyear program.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A concrete capex marker for utility trading modernization budgets — and a barrier that will force consolidation or capability outsourcing among mid-size traders.
insights.quote: The cost of this multiyear program could easily exceed $100 million.
insights.locator: Radical transformation means moving beyond incremental upgrades

insights.claim: Contrary to how most firms justify AI and automation, revenue gains are usually easier to realize and larger than cost savings — leading players can achieve gross margin improvements three to five times the size of potential cost savings in execution, mid- and back-office, IT, and support, with limited additional system cost.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Reframes the AI business case in trading from headcount cuts to alpha capture — a 3-5x ratio that should reset how investors value announced AI programs at trading houses.
insights.quote: leading players can achieve gross margin improvements three to five times the size of potential cost savings in execution, mid- and back-office, IT, and support activities
insights.locator: When deploying new advanced analytics, AI-enabled algorithms

insights.claim: Incremental modernization of trading systems delivers near-term improvements with less disruption but tends to reinforce fragmentation, limits the ability to scale advanced capabilities or fully embrace AI, and often ends in organizational frustration.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Read incremental IT roadmaps at utility trading arms as a negative signal — they lock in fragmentation rather than closing the gap to Citadel-class competitors.
insights.quote: The incremental path often leads to frustration within the organization.
insights.locator: Incremental modernization—upgrading selected parts

insights.claim: New entrants face a binary architecture choice: a large upfront build of a fully integrated data-centric platform that is cheaper over time, or a lean off-the-shelf stack that reaches market faster but will require a later, longer and costlier transformation.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Useful diligence lens on new energy-trading startups: the off-the-shelf route embeds a deferred, compounding technology liability that does not show up in early unit economics.
insights.locator: New or Smaller Entrants. These firms can design

themes.theme: Operating Model as the Real Constraint

insights.claim: BCG's 10-20-70 rule holds that only 10% of transformation value comes from new tools and 20% from modernizing technology, while 70% comes from changing the operating model and building new capabilities.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A reusable allocation heuristic: firms announcing tech spend without desk restructuring and incentive redesign are buying 30% of the available value at best.
insights.quote: 10% of the value comes from new tools, 20% from modernizing technology, and 70% from changing the operating model and building new capabilities
insights.locator: Culture and Operating Model Will Determine Who Wins

insights.claim: Capturing cross-portfolio value may require dismantling siloed desk structures even when those desks are performing well, because fragmented organizations cannot scale advanced capabilities and will lose competitiveness over time.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The hardest political act in energy trading is breaking profitable desks — firms unwilling to do it are the ones most likely to lose share to systematic entrants.
insights.quote: Executives should be especially vigilant about moving forward, even when change threatens existing profit centers or disrupts desks that are performing well.
insights.locator: They make transformation a front-office priority

insights.claim: Leading trading firms link performance and bonus participation to actual use of new shared tools and processes, holding traders, quants, analysts, and operations teams all accountable, because adoption does not happen without incentives.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Compensation linkage to tool adoption is a checkable, non-cosmetic marker of whether a trading firm's AI program is real.
insights.quote: Adoption does not happen without incentives.
insights.locator: They align incentives before deploying tools

insights.claim: Use-case-by-use-case AI deployment is a trap: it shows early wins but the real transformation never happens and the program fades before genuine technological change or AI adoption occurs.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Directly contradicts the standard 'start with pilots' playbook — treat pilot-heavy AI roadmaps at trading firms as evidence of stalled, not progressing, transformation.
insights.quote: A use-case by use-case deployment of new capabilities can seem attractive by starting small and showing first successes. Too often, however, the real transformation never happens.
insights.locator: They design end-to-end, not use-case by use-case

insights.claim: Successful programs retire legacy tools early and use clear top-down mandates to enforce adoption from day one, because trading organizations resist change most strongly when general performance looks strong.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Strong current trading P&L is itself a risk factor for transformation failure — good results delay the rebuild that determines 2035 competitiveness.
insights.quote: Trading organizations resist change, especially when general performance looks strong.
insights.locator: They create urgency, push for real change

insights.claim: There is no single blueprint for modernizing power and gas trading, but a ticking clock: firms investing now in data platforms, AI, operating model change, and end-to-end capabilities are the only ones prepared for the coming decade.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The closing framing sets a winner-take-most expectation for the 2026-2035 window — capability divergence, not commodity price, is the differentiator to track across energy traders.
insights.quote: Most everyone else is looking backward.
insights.locator: A single blueprint to modernize power and gas trading does not exist
